b: Is the worry over kids and smartphones a moral panic? — If not, what’s the real issue? And what is a moral panic anyway? Lorna Finlayson inquires

“There is no superlative strong enough for how this would transform mathematics, instantly unlocking a deluge of truths contingent upon the ambitious conjecture” — an AI may have proven the Riemann hypothesis

“As for ‘hopeful pessimism’, I’m afraid that pessimism generally outweighs my very conditional modicum of hope” — Lydia Davis is learning about Stoicism to help her think about the possible end of humanity
“Bentham’s body is still yielding new scientific insights” — Bentham’s head gets a CT scan. I’m sorry to report there is indeed a video
“Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic” — Thomas Nagel, interviewed about AI consciousness

“How you order and rank the different values in your life could be perfectly real and known at any moment, but you can’t forecast where your values will take you” — “This explains regret,” says Steven Hales

“It’s certain by next summer, the AI will be able to do most of those creative steps on its own and really do papers end to end… The summer after that, we won’t even understand what it’s doing” — AI in physics (via Kelly Truelove)
